newsitem.title: UK: CE Electric bid for Northern extended.
newsitem.headline: CE Electric bid for Northern extended.

text.p: U.S. group CE Electric, a unit of CalEnergy Co Inc, said late on Friday that its bid for British regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Electric had been extended until 1300 GMT on December 24.
It said the extension was made following a full hearing this evening of Britain's takeover panel.
"CE Electric understands that the reasons for the panel's decision will be published as soon as possible," it said.

The extension until Tuesday of the final 782 million pound takeover offer offer, which values Northern at 650 pence per share, appeared to underline that the fate of the bid was too close to call, analysts said.

Officials at the takeover panel declined to comment on the reasons for the extension, but the Financial Times reported that it had effectively stopped the clock on the battle because of accusations of irregularities in the conduct of the bid.

The Financial Times said it was beleived CE Electric, which had set a deadline of 1300 GMT on Friday for acceptances of its offer, had been close to declaring victory when the takeover panel launched a late-night inquiry into issues related to the bid.
The nail-biting bid has sparked furious arguments, with both companies protesting to the panel about each other's tactics.
Apart from Northern, there are just two independent Recs out of 12 set up at privatisation in 1990 -- Yorkshire and Southern.
